title: RIGHT JOIN
description: A RIGHT JOIN is a LEFT JOIN with the tables flipped: every row from the right table is kept, even without a match on the left. Write a query that returns every department's `name` alongside any employee's `first_name` in it, including departments with no employees (the employee name should be NULL).
hints: 💡 SQL concept to consider: RIGHT JOIN
employees RIGHT JOIN departments keeps every departments row, even a department with zero employees - that row just gets a NULL where the employee's name would be.
Select departments.name and employees.first_name, using employees RIGHT JOIN departments ON employees.department_id = departments.id (departments on the right).
expected_behavior: Returns one row per employee-department pairing, plus a row for any department with zero employees (employee name NULL).
solution: SELECT departments.name, employees.first_name FROM employees RIGHT JOIN departments ON employees.department_id = departments.id;
explanation: RIGHT JOIN is used far less often than LEFT JOIN in practice - most people just swap the table order and write a LEFT JOIN instead - but it's the same idea, mirrored: X RIGHT JOIN Y means "keep every row of Y."
